name: Jac
caption: You've been conditioned to confuse your status with your worth.

slides.text:
7 reasons people confuse social status with self-worth

(and why the black sheep stopped)

1. Status is visible. Worth isn't.

The world can see your car.

It can't see your character.

So we start polishing what people can SEE.

2. We were rewarded for ranking

Grades. Trophies. Likes.

From day one, being “better than” felt like being ENOUGH.

3. The feed is a scoreboard

Every scroll compares your life to someone's highlight reel.

And on a scoreboard, someone is always losing.

4. Admiration feels like love

When people admire your status, it feels like they value YOU.

It's not the same thing.

5. Status is easier to measure

You can count followers and money.

You can't count peace, honesty, or how you treat people.

6. The fear of being nobody

If your identity is your title,

losing it feels like losing YOURSELF.

7. Nobody taught us otherwise

Your worth isn't something you earn.

It's who you ARE before you do anything at all.

Status can be taken away.

Worth can't.

The black sheep stopped competing in a ranking they never agreed to.
